title: cold-start-probe-prefetch-econ-heuristics-2026
summary: Spreadsheet + notes for lightweight probe-based prefetch heuristics to reduce cold-start token spend. Combines microburst probe sampling, prefix-length bucketing, and probabilistic KV warming to estimate cost and latency tradeoffs.
assumptions: 1) Average request length after prompt: 120 tokens; 2) Cold KV miss adds 6ms per token on GPU (extra kernel path); 3) Prefetching costs counted as tokens charged at host rate; 4) Probe sample rate configurable per-client segment; 5) Prefetch window size measured in prefix tokens.
scenario_notes:
- 'probe_rate' is fraction of requests sampled to trigger a background prefetch.
- 'avg_prefetch_prefix' is how many prefix tokens we attempt to warm (rounded to cache page size).
- Hit rates are rough output of micro-sim; actual will vary by user behavior.
- Negative latency delta means median latency improved for warm requests; worst-case tail latency can worsen if prefetch competes for concurrency on small fleets.
- Cost numbers assume hosted API unit price $0.00008 per token generation equivalent (internal blended rate).
recommendations:
1) Run A/B with 2 segments: high-sensitivity (enterprise-commits) at probe_rate=0.01/prefetch=256 and conservative default at probe_rate=0.02/prefetch=64.
2) Instrument additional signals: session-id reuse, client SDK version, and latency tail before prefetch triggers.
3) Add safeties: cap concurrent prefetches per model pool and a token-budget throttle per customer to avoid noisy-neighbor prefetch storms.
4) Short-term: implement sampling probe and logging hooks (2-week experiment). Longer-term: adaptive probe based on measured hit-rate per 24h rolling window.
open_questions:
- What SLAs allow background prefetch if it increases CPU/GPU occupancy?
- Should prefetch tokens be charged as 'background' at discounted rate for enterprise customers?
- How to reconcile prefetch churn with KV cache eviction policy (LRU vs segmented)?

raw_simulation_notes:
Micro-sim approach: sample real request traces (1M requests), mark X% as probes, when probe hits do a background RPC to load KV pages up to prefix size, update simulated cache and compute token savings when subsequent requests hit. Sim runs use 30-day rolling trace slices and apply diurnal scaling.
Edge cases: extremely bursty tenants create prefetch churn and reduce net savings; short-lived sessions often wasted prefetch — consider session-length-based gating.
notes_to_reviewers: Focus review on sensitivity ranges for observed_hit_rate and operational safeguards. If you want to tune for median latency over cost, lower probe_rate and increase prefetch precision (use session-guided warming).
